evidence: read-only source audit; no implementation, device admission, GPU correctness or performance evidence for this proposed contract
purpose: Define a constrained first admission for ordered FFT radix decompositions with one logical register value per distinct radix; do not equate static checks with valid GPU plans.

existing_work.scope_warning: expanded_search/GENERATOR.md documents its older uniform R<=64 prototype. The later frontier_search/manifest.py:16 and frontier_search/candidate.hpp:30-48 allow uniform R<=256. Neither implementation admits this nonuniform contract; do not attribute frontier GPU evidence to the proposed domain.

candidate_contract.version: new explicit version, distinct from the uniform scalar-R request and candidate ID
candidate_contract.workload: CUDA, FP32, one-dimensional complex-to-complex forward, out-of-place, power-of-two N in 2..8192, batch in 1..65536, one upload and one kernel, effective registerBoost=1, no Rader, Bluestein, convolution, DCT, DST or R2C

fields.radix: ordered nonempty list of at most 32 entries, each in 2,4,8,16,32, with overflow-checked product exactly N
fields.register_table: exactly 33 integer slots indexed by radix 0..32; request identity and serialized canonical form include the complete table
fields.grouped_batch: positive power-of-two G dividing batch; actual block dimensions are scheduler-derived, not freely requested

table_profiles.nonuniform_active_only: each distinct active radix has one positive value and all inactive slots are exactly zero
table_profiles.uniform_compatibility: if all active values equal the same R, a separate explicit profile may reproduce current frontier's exact 33-slot table: supported radix 2,4,8,16,32 dividing R get R and all other slots zero, including unused supported slots as in frontier_search/candidate.hpp:51-59
table_profiles.reason: Freeze profile as part of the request and hash. No silent normalization between profiles: inactive nonzero entries may influence scheduling or recorded identity. An observed default outside either profile is unsupported identity, not a fabricated replay.

active_rules: For every distinct radix r in radix, R[r] is one of 2,4,8,16,32,64,128,256; r<=R[r]<=N, R[r] is divisible by r and N is divisible by R[r].

Compute minR and maxR over active stage entries, and require N divisible by minR and maxR divisible by each active R. In this proposed power-of-two profile the latter follows from the value set but must be checked explicitly.
Repeated occurrences of the same radix always use the same table slot and value; requests for different values for repeated equal-radix stages are unrepresentable and must be rejected.
The canonical candidate hash includes workload identity, ordered stages, profile, all 33 table slots and G, with a frozen unambiguous serialization.
candidate_contract.interpretation: These are conservative first-version constraints, not a necessary-and-sufficient characterization of VkFFT validity or hardware support. Logical R is not the physical CUDA register count.

scheduler_dependency_closure.injection: Replace the register-selection call at VkFFT/vkFFT/vkFFT/vkFFT_PlanManagement/vkFFT_HostFunctions/vkFFT_Scheduler.h:3015-3022 using the same exact-anchor, separate-generated-header technique as test/plan_selection_study/expanded_search/prepare_headers.py:31-50. Before downstream planning, derive the complete table, active multipliers and active min/max from the frozen request; preserve original unmodified path when no request is enabled.
scheduler_dependency_closure.freeze_order: First contract uses exact requested stage order. Suppress only the existing prototype's optimizer radix merges and min-R first-stage reorder for this path, retaining dependent usedLocRegs and non-power-of-two state derivation; compare requested and effective full sequence. If later upstream reorder is enabled, it is a separate contract with explicitly recorded effective order and fresh admission, not silent drift.
updates_to_audit: VkFFT/vkFFT/vkFFT/vkFFT_PlanManagement/vkFFT_HostFunctions/vkFFT_Scheduler.h:3101-3120 may scale min/max and all nonzero table entries to satisfy thread limits; reject any resulting difference from the frozen table rather than silently timing another request.

VkFFT/vkFFT/vkFFT/vkFFT_PlanManagement/vkFFT_HostFunctions/vkFFT_Scheduler.h:1958-1975 and :2001-2014 can merge multipliers and replace entries; :3200-3205 runs the optimizer and copies the table; :3230-3237 constructs stages.

VkFFT/vkFFT/vkFFT/vkFFT_PlanManagement/vkFFT_HostFunctions/vkFFT_Scheduler.h:2164-2203 MinMaxRegisterCheck reads nonzero active entries and updates min/max; it does not modify the table and does not itself reject a zero active entry. The call at :3256-3270 recomputes final min/max. Explicitly reject missing or zero active entries before it.

VkFFT/vkFFT/vkFFT/vkFFT_PlanManagement/vkFFT_HostFunctions/vkFFT_Scheduler.h:3281-3294 can move a minimum-R stage to the front. The existing expanded injection suppresses that change; exact-order admission must test both first- and last-stage IO consequences.

VkFFT/vkFFT/vkFFT/vkFFT_PlanManagement/vkFFT_HostFunctions/vkFFT_AxisBlockSplitter.h:261-266 uses min_registers_per_thread and can clamp; reject a clamped or otherwise mismatched actual dimension for this first contract.

Validate pre-codegen localSize against the then-current axisSwapped, and final normalized dispatch axisBlock separately after swap reset. Preserve actual values, not predicted layout as evidence.

Exercise both rising and falling R transitions and repeated radix; accepting divisibility alone does not prove index bounds.

Record and check actual readToRegisters/writeFromRegisters and both endpoints.
codegen_and_layout_dependencies.shared_memory: VkFFT/vkFFT/vkFFT/vkFFT_CodeGen/vkFFT_KernelsLevel0/vkFFT_MemoryManagement/vkFFT_MemoryInitialization/vkFFT_SharedMemory.h:48-51,78-99,161-171 computes padded stride and usedSharedMemory for actual geometry. G*N*complexSize is only a preliminary limit, not a proof of shared index bounds. Preserve planner/codegen derivation and verify actual compiled dynamic and static shared memory; an independent memory checking tool is needed for additional access-bound evidence.

reject_conditions: Malformed, missing, duplicate or ambiguous fields, integer overflow, unsupported workload/mode, conflicting old and new request interfaces, product not N, or noncanonical table profile.

Any unsupported radix, missing/zero active table entry, value outside the stated conservative domain, R[r] not divisible by r, N not divisible by required R or invalid repeated-radix per-stage override.

G not a power-of-two divisor of batch; predicted or actual thread/block geometry not matching the declared contract, an unsupported axis swap/dispatch normalization, device per-dimension or total block limit exceeded, or source-plan/actual-plan drift.

Unintended scheduler scale, table change, optimizer merge, stage-order change, active min/max mismatch, unsupported identity, source or compilation-option mismatch for an identity replay, or missing full requested/observed descriptors.

Compilation failure; dynamic shared memory exceeds function limit; dynamic plus static shared memory exceeds device limit; launch threads exceed device or compiled-function limit; execution failure or any numerical/reference/input-immutability check fails. Retain each rejection as a failure, not a latency observation.

Physical register pressure or local-memory spill alone is not an automatic numerical rejection: record compiled CUDA registers, local bytes and function limits, and require actual resource and correctness checks.

cpu_only: Test parser and canonical hash with ordered radix, complete tables and profile; reject missing, conflicting, malformed, zero, unsupported, overflow, product mismatch and impossible G; identical table with different stage order hashes differently.

Test min/max on active entries and explicit inactive profiles; assert repeated same radix cannot receive distinct values; check injected table, exact stage order and both pre-codegen/post-initialization actual descriptors, rejecting scheduler scaling or drift and changed upstream anchors.

Uniform compatibility profile must replay existing frontier uniform tables, including R=128/256 where N permits, and compare full descriptor, stages, geometry, generated-source hash and compiler inputs/options; this CPU comparison is not device correctness.
proposed_admission_matrix.same_device_gpu_prerequisite: Compare original default, new binary default and representable identity replay on the same device, full structure/table/source/options and resources; if unrepresentable, mark unsupported. Use GPU guard and independent original control without treating a failed identity as an admitted candidate.

nonuniform_cases.coverage: minimum R at tail, head and middle; repeated radix; rising and falling adjacent R
three active R values and larger max/min ratio

proposed_admission_matrix.case_qualification: These requests are proposed coverage examples, not assertions of scheduler acceptance, actual axis swap, compiled validity or numerical success. Actual eligible G and path coverage must be checked on the target device; add cases if desired IO/swap branches were not observed.
proposed_admission_matrix.per_case_correctness: After resource admission, use zero, impulse, constant, quarter-tone and random inputs for seeds 42,53,71; initialize output to NaN poison; verify input unchanged, single-forward and final output against an independent CPU reference for all batches and elements, including nonfinite and failure counts. Record effective stage order, complete table, min/max, localSize, axisSwapped, normalized axisBlock, group, read/write flags, shared bytes, source hash, compiler options, physical registers and local memory.
proposed_admission_matrix.performance: Only independently admitted exact requests may enter paired timing. Freeze the default comparator and candidate selection before timing, retain rejected and omitted points, and independently confirm selected winners; a correctness matrix is not performance evidence.

counterexamples.request: N=128, stages=[8,8,2], table={2:4,8:8}, G=1, claimed FFT threads=16
counterexamples.reason: Wrong: minR=4 so the restricted planned thread dimension is 128/4=32, not 128/maxR=16; reject mismatched actual layout.
R[8] is below radix 8 and not divisible by it.
An active table entry is zero; MinMaxRegisterCheck would skip it and cannot be relied upon to reject it.
R[2]=6 is outside the proposed power-of-two value profile; rejection is a conservative contract choice.

counterexamples.request: N=128, stages=[8,8,2], separate stage values for the two radix-8 stages of 8 and 16
counterexamples.reason: One table entry is indexed by radix; distinct stage-specific values cannot be represented.
G is not a power-of-two batch divisor in the proposed contract.

counterexamples.request: A valid request whose effective table is scaled by scheduler or whose order changes despite exact-order policy
counterexamples.reason: Reject the effective-plan mismatch and record it; do not label the modified plan as the requested candidate.

limitations: No source modifications, tests or GPU admission have been performed for this proposed contract. Exact-order suppression must itself be revalidated; support for mixed primes, boost>1, multi-upload or independently tuned equal-radix stages requires a separate model and admission.
